identity.title: Block corrected-output rerun while Step edit is unapplied

origin.kind: explicit user request and source review
origin.summary: The user authorized starting the next 2D pre-development slice from the current owner map. Source review found that the existing corrected-output rerun action remains executable while a selected Step PropertyGrid edit is dirty.

state.current_summary: PL-0058 remains resolved. The existing Local Validation Set contextual rerun regression also passes after the shared dirty guard, confirming the clean-state same-set branch is preserved.

claims.text: The corrected-output rerun command can remain executable while the selected Step edit session is dirty and unapplied.

problem.impact: An operator can believe the just-edited parameters were rerun even though the XML/pipeline still contains the previous saved values, weakening correction evidence and comparison trust.

criteria.text: RerunCorrectedOutputCommand.CanExecute returns false whenever the selected Step edit session is dirty, for both catalog Good/Bad and Local Validation Set contexts.
While dirty, CorrectedOutputRerunToolTipText tells the operator to apply or discard the pending Step edit; no Preview/Run or layer/routing mutation is triggered by the guard.
After a successful XML apply marks the edit clean, the existing contextual rerun command and its Good/Bad or same-set scope are restored unchanged.
The built corrected-output panel renders the disabled dirty state and readable tooltip/action text, and focused source/build/runtime checks pass with unrun theme/DPI states recorded.

evidence.observation: CanRerunCorrectedOutput only checks the selected run scope and CanRunLocalValidationSet/CanRunSelectedSamplePairCheck; it does not check IsSelectedStepEditDirty. The IsDirty property change does refresh command state, so the missing guard is observable as an enabled rerun path while dirty.
The source-built OpenVisionLab.sln Debug/Any CPU build completed with exit code 0, warnings 0, and errors 0 after the dirty-rerun guard change.

The focused WPF smoke target completed with exit code 0 and check=OK. Its runtime assertions observed IsEnabled=false and CanExecute=false with apply-before-rerun guidance while dirty, unchanged Preview/layer/route state until explicit XML apply, then restored the existing Good/Bad rerun and completed it successfully; layout=0, text=0, internal=0.

Fresh 1600x900 pending and applied corrected-output captures show the same Recipe Manager panel before and after XML apply. The pending capture shows the apply/discard guidance and disabled rerun affordance; the applied capture shows corrected-output guidance with the explicit rerun affordance restored.

The post-change rerun label/tooltip, defensive execution guard, and CanExecute guard all test IsSelectedStepEditDirty before the existing IsSelectedRunLocalValidationSet branch. The same safety boundary therefore covers both catalog Good/Bad and Local Validation Set rerun scopes; the focused runtime target exercises the catalog fallback and the source proof covers the shared branch ordering.

The existing p252 contextual Local Validation Set rerun target completed with exit code 0, check=OK, layout=0, text=0, and internal=0. The same-set rerun action remained enabled after a clean XML apply and preserved its persisted source-set and run-history contract.

events.summary: C1~C4 are satisfied by source, build, focused WPF runtime, and fresh visual evidence. Close PL-0058 without reopening completed owners; keep broader theme/DPI/input and field qualification outside this bounded slice.
